content:
**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected plant part**: Banana fruit (fingers/pods) — green, unripe
- **Visual features**:
  - Large, dark brown to black irregular necrotic lesions covering significant portions of the fruit surface
  - Lesions appear sunken and spreading, not confined to the tip
  - Distinct darkened patches on the green skin with rough, discolored texture
  - Two banana fingers affected, showing similar symptoms

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Cigar End Rot**: Causes dry, dark rot specifically at the distal *tip* of banana fingers (resembling a cigar end). The lesions here extend well beyond the tips onto the fruit body — doesn't match.
- **Bunchy Top**: Viral disease affecting the growing point and leaves (bunching of leaves at top). No fruit lesions — doesn't match.
- **Cordana Leaf Spot / Yellow & Black Sigatoka / Panama Disease**: These primarily affect leaves or the vascular system — not fruit surface lesions like these.
- **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum musae*): Causes dark, sunken, irregular lesions on banana fruit skin. Can appear on green fruit under favorable conditions. Lesions are dark brown to black, spreading across the fruit surface — this matches the image well.
